Indian police detain ‘cockroach’ movement leaders demanding election chief stand down

Reuters

13 October, 2026 07:30 pm IST

Facebook

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

NEW DELHI, Oct 13 (Reuters) – India’s “cockroach” youth movement leaders were detained on Tuesday after they jumped barricades to enter a historic Delhi site popular for protests, demanding that the chief election commissioner resign over a revision of voter lists.

Supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and opposition groups have held almost daily protests this month to demand commissioner Gyanesh Kumar stand down over the revisions critics say favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) by removing the names of millions of voters.

The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol, while the BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.

Show Full Article

Thousands joined a protest march by opposition groups on Monday, after a clampdown foiled CJP plans for a weekend demonstration, with police detaining thousands of protesters, including CJP leaders.

Delhi Police announced on Monday that the Jantar Mantar open air observatory, in the national capital’s central business district, was no longer designated as an official protest site, and said three new venues had been identified.

The CJP said its leaders Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das, and Ajinkya Shinde were among about 20 people who “sneaked” inside the observatory to “reclaim” it and were detained.

BIGGEST POLITICAL CHALLENGE FOR MODI

A CJP livestream showed about a dozen people jumping a gate and barricades to reach the site, where they waved the Indian flag and chanted slogans before police detained them.

Delhi Police did not respond to a request for comment.

The youth movement, which has mobilised protests in recent months against issues ranging from government school infrastructure to jobs, is among the biggest political challenges to Modi and his BJP in his 12 years in power.

A weeks-long sit-in by its supporters at Jantar Mantar earlier this year forced the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over exam paper leaks.

Sporadic demonstrations broke out elsewhere on Tuesday, including in Delhi’s business hub Connaught Place, where television footage showed dozens of members of the student unit of the main opposition Congress party being hauled into buses by police as they attempted to stage a sit-in protest.

A small group of protesters, including from left-wing student groups, tried to breach police barricades during a march in the eastern city of Patna.

Nearly 150 journalists gathered at the Press Club of India in New Delhi to march in protest against the detention of reporters covering events over the weekend.

The demonstrations erupted after the Indian Express newspaper reported last month that Kumar’s two deputies raised several concerns internally about voter list revisions, registration procedures and digital systems.

The change, which started last year, removed over 130 million names – more than the population of Japan – from voter lists, including 28 million who died, 63 million who relocated, and 30 million who could not be traced.

Opposition parties allege the deletions disproportionately affect Muslim voters and other minorities, who are unlikely to support the Hindu nationalist ruling party — allegations the poll panel and BJP reject.

(Reporting by Saurabh Sharma, Manoj Kumar and Adnan Abidi, writing by Sakshi Dayal, editing by Saad Sayeed, Alexandra Hudson)

Saudi-led coalition orders evacuation of Yemen oil facility in Sanaa ahead of operation

Reuters

13 October, 2026 07:00 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

By Tala Ramadan and Yomna Ehab Oct 13 (Reuters) – A Saudi-led coalition urged civilians on Tuesday to evacuate the Yemen Oil Company’s Sabah central station in the capital Sanaa ahead of a planned military operation.

A statement from the coalition’s joint forces command identified the site on a map and said civilians should leave the area for their own safety.

A military spokesperson for Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis, Yahya Saree, warned that any strikes on Sanaa would be met with a “harsh and painful” response in the Saudi capital Riyadh.

Show Full Article

The Houthis also warned employees and civilians near Saudi Aramco oil facilities to evacuate and stay away, saying the facilities were legitimate targets for their forces.

Fighting has escalated between the Saudi-led coalition and the Houthis, who have been attacking Saudi airports and oil facilities since last week in a spillover from the wider regional conflagration between the US and Iran.

Saudi Arabia has in recent weeks launched strikes against the Houthis and is backing a Yemeni government counteroffensive after the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.

The conflict has disrupted air travel in Saudi Arabia, with Riyadh airport remaining closed after a deadly missile strike on Saturday claimed by the Houthis.

(Reporting by Tala Ramadan and Yomna Ehab; Editing by Andrew Heavens and Andrwe Cawthorne)
